reader.requirement: At 85, after an unsuccessful input-output operation the run time executes the USE procedure naming the file (a) if one exists; otherwise the USE ON OUTPUT procedure when the file is open in, or being opened in, the output mode, and the USE ON EXTEND procedure for the extend mode (b, c), files named explicitly in another USE being excepted; and no mode procedure runs for a file in neither mode (a CLOSE of a file that is not open).

reader.notes: Selection is a file-name tier then an open-mode tier rendered once (UseTierEmitter) and fed by the connector's statement-scoped mode (the mode an OPEN attempts, the mode a CLOSE began in) and its opened mode; a completed CLOSE clears the mode, so a later CLOSE (42) selects no mode procedure. The 'unless an AT END phrase takes precedence' clause has no report-file statement to reach (report files are only opened OUTPUT/EXTEND and written by GENERATE). A GENERATE whose implicit WRITE fails could not be induced without exhausting the host and is not probed.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-243/runs): r3-orgs-002 (exit 0) with USE ON OUTPUT and USE ON EXTEND only: indexed DYNAMIC file OPEN OUTPUT, duplicate WRITE without INVALID KEY prints 'USE-OUTPUT' then 'W1-DUP-NOIK 22' (b, an indexed file open in the output mode); the same WRITE with INVALID KEY prints 'IK-BRANCH' and no USE (the phrase takes precedence); indexed SEQUENTIAL file OPEN EXTEND then an out-of-order WRITE prints 'USE-EXTEND' / 'EXT-W3 21' (c); a relative file OPEN I-O failing 35 and a sequential OPEN INPUT failing 35 run no procedure (neither output nor extend mode). r3-nested-001: a contained program's OPEN OUTPUT failing 30 does not run the containing program's non-GLOBAL USE ON OUTPUT ('INNER-OPEN 30' / 'BACK'), consistent with GR1's per-program scope. With the reader's report-file and sequential probes, a, b and c and the exclusion hold for every organization tried. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5' ('unless an AT END phrase takes precedence'); 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5b  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5b'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5c  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5c'. No edition site found on the path (the reader's grep; mode selection is edition-invariant), and nothing 1985-only to diverge on.
